subject: KPI Triage: leadership preflight for QBR — latency / cost / uptime / usage
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: KPI triage — initial dashboard ask for QBR preflight

Team —

I pulled the latest monthly KPI bundle for the upcoming QBR (link below) and flagged a few anomalies that I want us to triage before the pre-brief next week. High-level: latency median has a small uptick on the hosted API (p50 +9ms MoM), cost/unit increased ~6% for a subset of high-concurrency routes, and a couple of customers reported transient availability hits (two incidents in the 3rd week of Sep). Usage growth is healthy but noisy on the trial->paid transition for a large account (Acme).

Please see the attached PDF + csv for per-route breakdowns. For the preflight I need:
- Marissa: a short note on root cause hypotheses for the latency and cost increase and 2-3 mitigation options with estimated delta to unit cost.
- Markus: confirm SLO exposure and whether the uptick pushed any routes into a P1 risk window.
- Irene: leadership asks / any OKR-level implications if this trend continues for Oct.
- Tessa: owners + timelines for the quick wins we can present to execs at the QBR.

Deadline: EOD Tue (28 Sep) so we can synth a one-pager for the pre-brief Wed morning.

Attachments: monthly-kpi-dashboard-sep2026.pdf (dashboard export), latency-breakdown-sep2026.csv

Link: https://redwood.gdrive/reports/kpi-sep-2026

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Head of Platform Metrics | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI triage — initial dashboard ask for QBR preflight

Naomi —

Thanks for the flag and the artifacts. I dug into the latency-breakdown CSV and pulled a quick hypothesis thread:

1) Batch size/queueing changes on the hosted API during peak hours — the p95 and p99 spikes correlate with a change in continuous batching thresholds we rolled out in early Sep for cost savings. The p50 shift looks like side-effect when small requests now wait slightly longer to achieve efficient batch sizes.

2) Two routes with custom prompt templates (ads-ranking, multi-pass summarization) show 4–6% higher token counts versus the August baseline — that correlates to unit cost increase.

3) The availability blips (Acme reported) align with a brief autoscaler cold-start regression on a dedicated pool; root cause is an edge case in the scaling policy when mix of short-lived clients spikes.

Suggested mitigations (high level):
- For p50 latency: reduce min-batch delay for small-size routes (est. +4% cost) — fast to implement (2 d dev + 1 d canary).
- For cost-driven routes: apply prompt compression + caching on the multi-pass route (est. 8–12% cost reduction after rollout) — needs model/feature work (2 sprints).
- Autoscaler: patch the cold-start policy and add synthetic traffic during scale-down windows (est. reduces incidents to <1/mo) — quick patch + 1-week monitoring window.

I attached a short CSV slice with route-level delta and proposed owner column. Will expand into a 1-pager if this direction looks right.

Attachments: latency-breakdown-sep2026.csv (annotated slice)

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Platform Metrics | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Sara Bishop <sara.bishop@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: support@acme.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI triage — initial dashboard ask for QBR preflight

Hi Naomi / Marissa —

Quick note from the Acme side: we saw two short outages during the week of Sep 13. Symptoms: 503 responses for ~90s and timeouts on batch jobs that run nightly. We restarted a few client tasks which recovered the jobs. We did capture a few request ids which I can share if helpful. Happy to brief during the QBR — this did impact two major batch workflows, but the realtime API remained healthy.

Thanks,
Sara Bishop
Head of Data Platform | Acme Corp
sara.bishop@acme.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 11:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI triage — initial dashboard ask for QBR preflight

Team —

I validated SLO exposure: the two routes Marissa called out crossed the soft threshold for our internal P2 boundary during the Sep 13 spike; no hard P1 breaches on the hosted control plane. The dedicated pool incident for Acme is the higher concern because it touched customer-facing batch SLA windows.

Immediate asks:
- Ops to enable higher replicant floor for that dedicated pool for the next 72 hours while we patch the autoscaler behavior.
- Incident runbook: request Sara's request ids (Sara: can you share them via this thread or a secure drive?)

I'll start the patch now; ETA for a staged rollout is 36 hours. If we see regression in costs after raising the replicant floor, we can revert the change and apply targeted throttles.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Site Reliability | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI triage — initial dashboard ask for QBR preflight

Thanks all — great triage thread. Two leadership-level notes for the pre-brief:

1) Framing: present this as a capacity/optimization tradeoff (small p50 regressions from batching vs. overall cost savings) and a targeted reliability incident (Acme dedicated pool). That allows us to propose both short-term mitigations and a longer-term guardrail.

2) OKR implications: if the multi-pass/caching initiative slips, we risk missing our Q4 cost-per-token efficiency target by 1–2 pts. I want Marissa to include a slide with the rollout timeline and the minimal MVP change that preserves >75% of estimated savings.

3) Ask for exec decision: authorize a temporary replicant floor increase for the Acme pool for 72h (Markus's recommendation) and approve a 2-week fast-track for the caching work on the multi-pass route (dedicated feature resource). We should show the estimated net cost delta and customer risk trade-off on one slide.

Tessa — please produce an owner/timeline table and a short script for the pre-brief by Wed 09:00 PT. Naomi — I'll join the pre-brief.

Irene Choi
VP, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
